names.name: Cal-Neva Lodge
names.operator: Robert P. Sherman (builder); Norman Blitz; investor group with William Remmer from 1935
names.note: Built 1926; burned and rebuilt in 1937; legal gambling from 1931

names.name: Cal Neva Lodge
names.note: Bought from Remmer for $700,000; hyphen dropped (Wikipedia: c. end of WWII; spelling already in use earlier)

names.name: Cal Neva Lodge
names.note: Bought March 21, 1955 for $1 million

names.name: Cal Neva Lodge
names.operator: Park Lake Enterprises (Frank Sinatra, Hank Sanicola, Paul D'Amato and others); leased to Jack Warner
names.note: Sinatra surrendered his Nevada gaming licences in 1963 after Giancana was found there; AP gives 1960-1963 as his ownership years, Wikipedia says the property was sold in 1968

names.name: Cal Neva Lodge
names.operator: Owners of Reno's Club Cal Neva; later Ohio Real Estate Investment Trust (1970); federal receivership 1973
names.note: Ten-story expansion 1969; winter closure 1974

names.name: Cal Neva Lodge
names.operator: BKJ Corporation (licence refused); First National Bank of Nevada; Kirk Kerkorian (Tracinda) from 1976
names.note: Foreclosure early 1976; a 1985 fraud buyer was arrested

names.name: Cal Neva Resort & Casino
names.operator: Chuck Bluth (1985); Ezri Namvar (2005); Canyon Capital foreclosure
names.note: Casino shut down in April 2010; resort closed Sept 2013 for renovation

names.name: Cal Neva Lodge
names.note: Bought April 2013; bankruptcy 2016; sold at auction Jan 2018; McWhinney April 2023 to convert to a hotel

label.basis: A historian, an oral-history volume and an FBI file record that Giancana, on Nevada's excluded list, was a guest at the Cal-Neva and that Sinatra surrendered his licences in 1963; Giancana's ownership is only informant reporting and Sinatra denied it.

venues.corrections: (1) The record says Sinatra 'partnered with' Giancana: sources I opened document Giancana as a guest and Sinatra's licence surrender (1963); joint ownership appears only as unverified FBI informant reporting and a rumor, and Sinatra denied it, so that part is alleged. (2) Wikipedia says licence 'suspended'; the sources say surrendered. (3) 'Closed 2013' is the resort; the casino stopped in April 2010. (4) Sinatra's ownership 1960 to 1963 (AP) vs sale in 1968 (Wikipedia): the record should say 1960-1968 with licence lost 1963.

names.name: Harold's Club (later Harolds Club)
names.operator: Harold S. Smith Sr. and Raymond A. Smith; Raymond I. 'Pappy' Smith as manager
names.note: Opened Feb 23, 1935; apostrophe dropped over time

names.name: Harolds Club
names.note: 1962 sale of the property for $16.5 million and 25-year leaseback

names.name: Harolds Club
names.note: Sold June 1970 (Wikipedia: $11.5 million); $20 million expansion 1971

names.name: Harolds Club
names.operator: The Fitzgerald Group of Reno; Gamma International (American Gaming and Entertainment) 1995
names.note: Closed March 31, 1995; reopened four hours in 1997 to keep its licence

names.name: Site (Harrah's Plaza)
names.note: Bought 1999; imploded December 1999; outdoor plaza

label.basis: The sources opened describe a family-run club with an honest-game reputation and show no court, board or congressional finding of organised-crime ties; the Kefauver index text search found no entry.

venues.corrections: The record says 'family-owned throughout its history': wrong. The Smiths sold to Howard Hughes in June 1970, then The Fitzgerald Group (1988) and Gamma International (1995). Demolition was December 1999 (Online Nevada: Dec 16; Sun: Dec 15).

names.name: Bingo parlors and bar (Plaza Tango / Heart Tango)
names.operator: William F. Harrah in joint ventures
names.note: First bingo parlor Oct 1937; small-time operations until 1946

names.name: Harrah's Reno Club (Harrah's Club)
names.note: Absorbed neighbours, including Pick Hobson's Frontier Club in 1956

names.name: Harrah's Reno (Golden Hotel tower)
names.operator: Harrah's (William F. Harrah to 1978; company public 1971, NYSE 1973)
names.note: Golden Hotel bought 1968; 24-story tower opened Oct 10, 1969

names.name: Harrah's Reno
names.operator: Holiday Inns, then Promus Hotel Company
names.note: Holiday Inns acquired the company in 1980; Promus spin-off 1995

names.name: Harrah's Reno
names.note: Bought the adjoining Harold's Club and Nevada Club 1999

names.name: Harrah's Reno
names.operator: VICI Properties (owner), leased to Caesars Entertainment
names.note: Closed March 17, 2020; Caesars said in June 2020 it would not reopen

names.name: Reno City Center
names.note: Sale completed Sept 2020; conversion to apartments and mixed use

label.basis: No source I opened shows an organised-crime link; a company oral history reports Harrah's persuaded financiers it was not mob-owned, and a Kefauver index text search found no entry.

venues.corrections: The record has closed: null. The property closed March 17, 2020 and was not reopened. The 1937 opening is a small bingo parlor that closed within months; Harrah's casino (Harrah's Reno Club) dates from 1946.

names.name: Mapes Hotel
names.note: Opened Dec 17, 1947; casino closed Dec 17, 1982

names.name: Mapes Hotel (vacant)
names.note: Mapes could not repay $15 million; foreclosed December 1982

names.name: Mapes Hotel (vacant)
names.note: Bought June 1988; never reopened

names.name: Mapes Hotel (vacant)
names.note: Imploded January 30, 2000; site now park and ice rink

label.basis: Sources opened show family ownership and a bank foreclosure with no organised-crime allegation; the only congressional trace is a hearings-index entry whose context I did not open.

venues.corrections: Dates are confirmed. Note the casino closed in 1982 but the building stood until the January 2000 demolition.

gaps: Cal Neva opening (1926) rests on Wikipedia; no primary or archival source opened.
Cal Neva: the full Gaming Control Board complaint and Nevada Gaming Commission minutes were not opened; vault.fbi.gov page itself was not opened (archive.org copy of the file used).
Cal Neva: the FBI file's shareholder list (Sinatra 36.6 percent in Park Lake) and Chicago-office 'jointly owned' note are OCR-garbled; recalled, not fetched as a clean quote.
